title: Impresarios who match musicians; all-star bands
summary: He complains that impresarios kill bandleaders by matching musicians.

bands.name: Louis Jordan and His Tympany Five

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I wish I could get old George to see that...I mean...
Has George ever heard her sing?

Those guys, they don't have--how to measure anything. They have no measurement of concept. That's why they match up musicians in the (unintelligible). I'm not saying George would, himself, but others. But I wish impresarios would stop matching musicians. And let the musician get the musicians that they can play with.

Because what it's done...it has killed band leaders. They don't have any organized small groups. Years ago you had the Savoy Saltons, Louis Jordan's Tympany Five, you know... you name it and you had a group. But today you don't have any of that.
All you have is All Stars...
Sammy Price and Friends. So some guy says, 'Sammy Price is playing with some of his friends, and some of them are his enemies. (Laughter).
